conviction_note: Scaled number = (2*0.54-1)*13 = +1.04: a small positive lean from two company-level documents (a habit of printing above its own revenue range, and IEEPA tariff refunds received after June 30 that the CFO said are NOT in the Q1 or FY27 forecast), held near 50 by a +21-vol-point put skew, a +16% 20-day run-up into the print and a reaction history in which beats were sold when the guide disappointed (Aug 2026 -15.6%). The findings sum to +1.4, close to the scaled number; the stock trades on the FY27 guide ($2.3-2.4bn), and nothing found decides that sign.
bar: Q1 FY27 revenue: company guide $545-565m (midpoint $555m), Q4 FY26 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639825/000163982526000032/q4fy2026earningspressrelea.htm ; consensus $555.77m (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PTON) and $553.8m (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PTON/earnings-forecasts), which agree with the guide midpoint. Also guided: adj. EBITDA $135-145m, gross margin ~57.0%, ending paid connected-fitness subs 2.455-2.475m; FY27 revenue $2.3-2.4bn, adj. EBITDA $475-525m, FCF >= $350m. EPS consensus disputed ($0.11 EW vs $0.14 Benzinga), so not used as the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 60,928,143 shares, 14.07% of float, 7.0 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 record date, down 9.47% from 67,303,087 on 2026-09-30 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/PTON/short-interest/). Shorts were covering into a +16.0% 20-day / +6.7% 5-day run-up. Skew +21.44 vol points (25d put IV over call IV): the option market pays for downside; put/call OI ratio 0.33. Event-implied move 12.41% against a median prior reaction of 12.01%. A crowded-ish short is a reason to shrink negatives; the skew is a reason to keep any long lean small.

findings.finding: Peloton routinely prints revenue above the top of its own range: Q1 FY26 revenue $550.8m was $6m above the high end of guidance, FY26 revenue $2,446.0m was $6m above the range, and Q3 FY26 beat guidance on equipment sales. The same habit applied to the Q1 FY27 range of $545-565m implies about $565-571m against a consensus of $554-556m (the guide midpoint), i.e. +2-3% on revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats did not decide the reaction: Q1 FY26 (Nov 2025) beat + upbeat holiday outlook +14.2%; Q4 FY26 (Aug 2026) beat but weak FY27 guide -15.6%; Q2 FY26 (Feb 2026) -25.7% on the outlook. The beat is paid only when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($555.77m EW, $553.8m Benzinga) rather than at the top of the range where the company has actually landed; if the street had priced the habit, the estimates would sit at $565m or above. Partly priced, because the pattern is visible to anyone who reads three releases.
findings.independence: FY26 beat-the-range figure from the Q4 FY26 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639825/000163982526000032/q4fy2026earningspressrelea.htm (a different document).

findings.finding: The FY26 10-K says 'Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the Company began to receive refund payments for IEEPA tariffs previously paid' and that it will recognise refunds 'when they are realized or realizable'; the CFO said on the Aug 6 call that $3m had been received and that refunds were 'not incorporated into our forecast for the quarter or year'. So any refunds realised in July-September 2026 land in Q1 FY27 on top of a guide (gross margin ~57%, adj. EBITDA $135-145m) that excludes them. Amount not disclosed; FY26 total tariff exposure was estimated at about $30m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Peloton print has carried a tariff refund. The path to the multiple is FY27 FCF (guided at >= $350m) and adj. EBITDA if refunds keep coming; if the company folds them into a raised EBITDA/FCF outlook this becomes a guidance item. On other names in this repo refund landings split by guidance direction.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EBITDA and margin are anchored to a guide the CFO said excludes refunds; if the market had priced the refunds, revenue-neutral estimates of gross margin/EBITDA would sit above the guided 57% / $140m midpoint. The amount is undisclosed, so no model can carry a number.
findings.independence: CFO quote reported by PeloBuddy, 2026-08-19, https://www.pelobuddy.com/?p=45107 (same event, the call, not the 10-K text). Shares the company as source; one fact, counted once.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 churn spiked to 2.2% (up 100bps q/q); management attributed about half of the involuntary-churn increase to a one-time change in failed-payment email timing, said it reverted the change and that involuntary churn had begun to normalise. A normalising churn rate would put ending subs at or above the top of the 2.455-2.475m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber beats are small and habitual (Q1 FY26 ended 2,000 above the top of guidance); the stock has not moved on them, it moved on the outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management told the market and the sub guide was set after the reversal. What would show it unpriced is a sub consensus below the guide range; none was found. Sized near zero because it lands inside what the company already guided.
findings.independence: Q4 FY26 8-K shows the 2.2% churn and 2.553m ending subs, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639825/000163982526000032/q4fy2026earningspressrelea.htm

findings.finding: Peloton launched the Tread Flex on 2026-09-22 at $2,195, its cheapest treadmill and first folding model, with North American shipments from 2026-10-01, alongside a revamped Tread line and AI coaching; this is the main new hardware for the holiday (Q2) quarter and gives management a concrete reason to hold or firm the FY27 revenue outlook ($2.3-2.4bn) on the Nov 5 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line this stock trades on: +14.2% (Nov 2025, upbeat holiday outlook after a hardware refresh), -25.7% (Feb 2026, weak demand outlook), -15.6% (Aug 2026, FY27 revenue decline guide).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for six weeks, so the launch is known; what is not known is early sell-through, which only the call reveals. Inference: the FY27 guide was set on Aug 6 and probably already assumed the launch, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Pricing and Oct 1 ship date from SlashGear, https://www.slashgear.com/2265260/peloton-treadmill-price-tread-flex-how-much-cost-first-foldable-model/ (same launch, different reporter).

findings.finding: Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig (interim CFO Mar-Jun 2026) resigned per an 8-K dated 2026-10-08/13, staying until 2026-11-27 for an outside opportunity, the third senior finance change in 2026 after CFO Liz Coddington left (Mar) and Siddharth Thacker joined (Jun).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reaction found to the 8-K; the stock rose about 16% over the 20 sessions after it.
findings.why_not_priced: Public filing, so it is in the price as a fact; it was filed without severance and with an orderly handover through the close, which is why the market ignored it. Sized small: it bears on reporting quality only if the release carries a restatement or control item.

findings.finding: Short interest 60.9m shares (14.07% of float, 7.0 days to cover) at 2026-10-15, down 9.5% from 67.3m at 2026-09-30, while the stock ran up 16% in 20 days: shorts are covering into the print but a 14%-of-float short base remains as fuel on any guide hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 (short base ~72.7m, 5.9 days) the upbeat print bought +14.2%; the run-up into this print cuts the other way, because it raises the bar a hold of the guide has to clear.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own statement; the +21 vol-point put skew shows the option market leaning down despite the short base. Sized small and positive only because a 14% short with 7 days to cover is a squeeze mechanism the skew does not net out.
findings.independence: Earlier FINRA readings via Equibles (61.1m, 8.9 days, Aug 2026), https://equibles.com/stocks/pton/shortinterest

findings.finding: An independent series on the end market is soft: Grips Intelligence puts tracked online home-fitness-equipment sales at $919m in 2025, down 5-10%, and expects a further 5-10% decline in 2026; Peloton itself acknowledged continued softness in US connected-fitness demand in May 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Weak demand commentary drove the Feb 2026 -25.7% reaction (Q3 revenue guided below the street on weak equipment demand).
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy, not a Peloton number; the FY27 guide of -3.9% already assumes declining hardware, so this is mostly priced. Shrunk further for the 14% short base.
findings.independence: Peloton Q3 FY26 call remark on US connected-fitness softness, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/peloton-interactive-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-05-08/

findings.finding: Section 122 tariffs of 10% expired 2026-07-23 and new Section 301 tariffs of 10.0-12.5% took effect 2026-07-24 on Peloton's contract-manufactured imports (10-K subsequent-events text), so a running tariff cost continues in Q1 even as IEEPA refunds come back.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff cost estimates moved down ($45m to $30m for FY26) at the May 2026 print, which rose +8.9%; no clean reaction to tariff costs alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the guide: the Q1 gross-margin guide of ~57% was set on Aug 6, after the Section 301 tariffs took effect, so the company told the market to expect it. Sized near zero.
findings.independence: Shares the 10-K with the IEEPA refund finding (different passage, opposite sign; both can be true).

outside_window.finding: Commercial Series (heavy-use gym bike and treadmill under Precor) begins shipping 'late 2026'; revenue effect falls in later quarters.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Front Office Sports piece labelled 'Tuesday, October 13, 2026': Peloton cuts hardware prices and hikes subscription
rejected_candidates.detail: The article itself is dated 2022-04-14; the 2026 date was the site's page date, not the story's.
Dated 2026-01-30 per the URL path; its savings are already in the FY26 results and the restructuring is 'substantially implemented' per the Q4 FY26 8-K, so it adds nothing new for this print.

rejected_candidates.detail: The page itself shows $0.11; Benzinga shows $0.14; EPS bar treated as disputed and not used.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean cuts against the +21 vol-point put skew and follows a +16% run-up that raises the bar, so p_up is held at 54, not higher; the 14% short base is the one positioning fact on the long side.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold the Aug 2026 beat): the beat-the-range finding went from +1.0 to +0.5, and p_up from 56 to 54.

Lesson 2 (one-offs): the IEEPA refund stays filed as one_off and went from +1.0 to +0.7. It is kept above a pure fraction because the 10-K recognition policy matches a disbursement that began after June 30, and the CFO said the guide excludes it. That is the 'what has worked' pattern.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): churn normalisation went from +0.5 to +0.2 and Section 301 tariffs from -0.2 to -0.1, because both were told to the market before the guide was set.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, 14% of float): the negative end-market proxy went from -0.5 to -0.3, and the CAO departure from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller, but filed): the Grips Intelligence series stays filed as a small proxy.
The Tread Flex guidance finding (+0.3 from +0.5), the positioning finding (+0.3) and abs_move_pct (13) are otherwise unchanged in kind.
